correctness.rationale: An odd-length bit string cannot equal its reverse complement at the middle bit; sixteen required classes need sixteen windows, hence at least twenty bits. An independently written exhaustive check visited all 2^20 literal words, found 512 covers and none with unequal four-bit ends, and recovered 32 rotation classes, eight four-element complement/reversal orbits, and exactly the eight listed representatives. Replay: /workspace/branches/6cec91fc-00bc-4cd0-a625-2fc23d0aff53/independent_enumeration.py; saved chunk evidence: independent_chunks.jsonl in that directory. The analytic closure argument is also valid: the selected and reverse-complemented edges partition the directed order-five edge set (and likewise at every odd order for a tight cover); each vertex imbalance equals that of its partner and is even at a fixed vertex. The imbalance +1 of an open trail is therefore impossible. Each cycle has full period sixteen because otherwise a window class would repeat. Each literal cover is a cut extended by its starting four bits, giving exactly sixteen cuts per rotation class. In the frozen Euler-tour route, a choice of orientation fixes one edge per pair, the balance/connectivity tests are the Euler conditions, and choosing the only used edge from (00000,11111) as first breaks rotations uniquely. The frozen code and recorded output were inspected; the independent enumeration did not execute either frozen algorithm.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Optimal linear words correspond to cuts of primitive half-cycles, not to full order-five de Bruijn circles. Each qualifying half-cycle can be joined to its reverse complement at any of the four reverse-complement-fixed four-bit vertices: its selected in/outdegrees are both one there. Conversely a full CR-invariant circle has a unique edge reflection (a second would give a nontrivial rotational symmetry, impossible for distinct edges). The two half-trails between the axes are reverse-complement partners with one edge per pair; closure makes their common joining vertex fixed. Thus the full rotation-class count is twice the half-circle count, not equal to it. A full-cycle count would be relevant, but an explicit example or divisibility alone does not give that number.

value.rationale: At the first nontrivial odd binary size with these multiple equality types, the classification tells how many optimizers actually exist and separates all their symmetry orbits rather than supplying one construction. The census yields a useful exact small-order benchmark for strand-symmetric binary cover structure; the parity argument explains why tight words can all be classified as circular cuts, independently of exhaustive computation.
